data.title: First-Party Credit Buildup and Sudden Spike
data.description: Detects consumer accounts following a first-party fraud pattern: steady good payments for 6-12 months then sudden utilization spike and missed payments within 60 days. Unlike synthetic identity (TP-0003), the identity is real but the intent is fraudulent. First-party bust-out actors nurture credit profiles with consistent on-time payments and low utilization, then rapidly maximize available credit before abandoning the account. The transition from responsible usage to aggressive drawdown is the key behavioral signal. LexisNexis estimates first-party fraud now represents 36% of all detected fraud events globally.

detection.condition: selection AND filter_good_history AND filter_utilization_spike AND filter_missed_payment

enrichment_required.source: Consecutive on-time payment count from credit bureau or internal payment history
Rolling average utilization over prior 6-month window
Derived from payment due dates and payment receipt records
Derived from utilization crossing 85% threshold date

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for First-Party Credit Buildup and Sudden Spike
// Detects bust-out pattern: 6+ months good payments then spike and missed payment
(account_type="consumer_credit" OR account_type="credit_card")
on_time_payment_months>=6
previous_avg_utilization_pct<40
current_utilization_pct>=85
days_since_first_missed_payment<=60
days_since_utilization_spike<=60
| utilization_jump_pct := current_utilization_pct - previous_avg_utilization_pct
| payment_behavior_change_flag := if(days_since_first_missed_payment <= days_since_utilization_spike, "spike_then_miss", "miss_then_spike")
| groupBy(account_id, function=[
    collect([credit_limit, current_balance, current_utilization_pct,
             previous_avg_utilization_pct, utilization_jump_pct,
             on_time_payment_months, days_since_first_missed_payment,
             account_open_date])
  ])
| sort(utilization_jump_pct, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for First-Party Credit Buildup and Sudden Spike")`
`comment("Detects 6+ months good payments followed by utilization spike and missed payment")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:credit_monitoring
  (account_type="consumer_credit" OR account_type="credit_card")
  on_time_payment_months>=6
  previous_avg_utilization_pct<40
  current_utilization_pct>=85
  days_since_first_missed_payment<=60
  days_since_utilization_spike<=60
| eval utilization_jump = current_utilization_pct - previous_avg_utilization_pct
| eval risk_score = case(
    utilization_jump > 60 AND on_time_payment_months >= 12, "critical",
    utilization_jump > 45, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table account_id, account_type, credit_limit, current_balance,
        current_utilization_pct, previous_avg_utilization_pct,
        utilization_jump, on_time_payment_months,
        days_since_first_missed_payment, account_open_date, risk_score
| sort - utilization_jump
queries.sql:
-- SQL for First-Party Credit Buildup and Sudden Spike
-- Detects bust-out pattern: good payment history then sudden spike and missed payment
SELECT
  a.account_id,
  a.account_type,
  a.credit_limit,
  a.current_balance,
  a.current_utilization_pct,
  h.previous_avg_utilization_pct,
  (a.current_utilization_pct - h.previous_avg_utilization_pct) AS utilization_jump,
  p.on_time_payment_months,
  DATEDIFF(DAY, p.first_missed_payment_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS days_since_first_missed_payment,
  a.account_open_date,
  DATEDIFF(MONTH, a.account_open_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS account_age_months
FROM credit_accounts a
JOIN credit_utilization_history h ON a.account_id = h.account_id
JOIN payment_history p ON a.account_id = p.account_id
WHERE a.account_type IN ('consumer_credit', 'credit_card')
  AND p.on_time_payment_months >= 6
  AND h.previous_avg_utilization_pct < 40
  AND a.current_utilization_pct >= 85
  AND p.first_missed_payment_date IS NOT NULL
  AND DATEDIFF(DAY, p.first_missed_payment_date, CURRENT_DATE) <= 60
ORDER BY utilization_jump DESC

references: LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Global State of Fraud and Identity Report (2026)
Federal Reserve, Synthetic Identity Fraud in the U.S. Payment System (2024)
Aite-Novarica Group, First-Party Fraud: The Growing Challenge (2023)
falsepositives: Legitimate financial hardship (job loss, medical emergency) causing simultaneous high spending and missed payments
Consumers running up balances during planned bankruptcy filing
Balance transfer activity creating temporary utilization spike on source account
